listed_sector_signals.signal: MCDM framework empirically applied as a case study to a real petrochemical complex in Egypt
listed_sector_signals.quote:
A comparative analysis using a case study of a petrochemical complex in
Egypt demonstrated that FAHP-VIKOR and FAHP-TOPSIS are consistent, robust, and simple to implement.

listed_sector_signals.signal: Petrochemical industry described as continuous transformation of oil and gas into plastics, fertilizers, etc.
listed_sector_signals.quote:
The petrochemical industry transforms oil and gas into many other
products such as plastics, clothing, detergents, and fertilizers.

listed_sector_signals.signal: Framework applied to an actual Egyptian petrochemical complex operating under ISO 50001 with identified EEPs
listed_sector_signals.quote:
The proposed framework for evaluating EEPs was applied in this case
study to an Egyptian petrochemical complex (the name of the firm is not
provided for confidentiality reasons).

listed_sector_signals.signal: EEPs involving ethylene boilers, cracked gas compressors and cracking furnaces (olefins/ethylene production equipment)
listed_sector_signals.quote:
Improve ethylene boiler efficiencies by improving control, cleaning, and
reducing losses

listed_sector_signals.signal: EEP to reduce blowdown from cracking furnaces (continuous ethylene cracking)
listed_sector_signals.quote:
Replacement of the blowdown valves to reduce blowdown from cracking
furnaces

listed_sector_signals.signal: Steam system identified as central to the petrochemical production process in the case study ranking
listed_sector_signals.quote:
the three highest-ranked
projects have connections to the steam system that plays a substantial
role in the petrochemical industry.

one_line: The paper develops a two-stage FAHP-MCDM framework for prioritizing energy-efficiency projects and empirically applies it to a real Egyptian petrochemical complex (with ethylene boilers, cracking furnaces, cracked gas compressors, and steam systems), plus comparison firms in Ireland and Qatar.
